$doc: Vyomi capability registry — GCP Artifact Registry. One entry per console section; level per substrate (nano = shared core, also dev_server/unified ingress; offline = appliance). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py — a claim the backend does not honour fails CI.

gcp.artifacts.push-sample.title: Push sample image/package
limitations: Vyomi has no Docker/Maven/npm/pip daemon, so repositories can't be populated by a real `docker push` et al.; this console action creates a sample package/version directly so the console has real data to show.
api: repositories.pushSample (Vyomi-only convenience; not a real Artifact Registry method)

gcp.artifacts.iam.title: Permissions (IAM policy)
limitations: getIamPolicy/setIamPolicy/testIamPermissions store and return the policy exactly as configured; Vyomi does not authenticate requests or enforce the bindings.

gcp.artifacts.encryption.title: Encryption (customer-managed key)
limitations: A customer-managed key resource name is stored on the repository and returned by the API; Vyomi does not verify the key exists or encrypt stored data with it.

gcp.artifacts.repository-mode.title: Repository mode (remote / virtual)
limitations: A virtual repository's upstream policies are enforced: its packages/versions/tags/images are a live, priority-ordered aggregate of its member (standard/remote) repositories in the same location, and it rejects direct pushes/deletes since it has none of its own. Remote repositories still only store their config — proxying a real upstream (Docker Hub, npm, Maven Central, …) needs real network egress to a third-party registry, which Vyomi does not perform.

gcp.artifacts.cleanup-policies.title: Cleanup policies
limitations: Cleanup policies are enforced, not just stored: a DELETE policy's olderThan/newerThan/tagState/packageNamePrefixes/versionNamePrefixes conditions are evaluated against real package versions (lazily, the next time the repository is read or written, rather than on the real product's periodic schedule), and matching versions are actually deleted unless a KEEP policy protects them. cleanupPolicyDryRun is honoured (nothing is deleted) but Vyomi does not produce the real product's Cloud Logging dry-run preview report, and the mostRecentVersions (keep-N) policy variant is not modeled.

gcp.artifacts.vulnerability-scanning.title: Vulnerability scanning (Artifact Analysis)
limitations: The vulnerability-scanning setting is stored on the repository and returned by the API; Vyomi does not scan images or report findings.
